feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — Copyright law is not a bounded object; it is an abstract legal system.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — A constructed legal framework developed through human invention.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Not biologically inspired or modeled.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Does not depend on an energy source.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — It is abstract and not physically load-bearing.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — Only instantiated via documents or speech acts.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — Exists across media but is not defined by materiality.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires enforcement bodies and agents to act.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Deliberately created to regulate intellectual property rights with defined purposes and boundaries.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Effects are downstream through application, not inherent to the law itself.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Not a logic-processing system, but a symbolic structure.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — It may enable changes in status but does not change internal state.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Interpreted and enforced by humans, but not interactive by design.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — It governs systems but is not a subsystem within one.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Has no operative function without human institutions.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Intellectual property systems can exist in informal or customary forms.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Expresses rights, limits, and permissions symbolically through legal text.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Communicates legal boundaries, ownership, and use permissions.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Composed entirely of codified, interpretable rules.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Structured into articles, clauses, and exceptions that function together.
feedback.Normative: Included — Prescribes behaviors and constrains use of creative works.
feedback.Meta: Included — Contains clauses that regulate how its own rules are applied, interpreted, and changed.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Defines limited durations of protection and structured renewal windows.
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Exists primarily in digital legal databases, statutes, and licensing APIs.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists by collective agreement and institutional authority.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Defined and enforced by governments and legal systems.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — Tied to the identity of authors, creators, and rightsholders.
feedback.Regulated: Included — It is itself a formal regulatory system.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Central to industries like publishing, software, entertainment, and media.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Heavily shaped by lobbying, ideology, and international treaty negotiations.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — Enforced through repeatable legal procedures (e.g., filings, lawsuits, cease-and-desist letters).
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Touches on fairness, ownership, public access, and cultural rights.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats copyright law as a formal legal abstraction: synthetic, designed, rule-based, and temporally structured. Its identity is defined by institutional enforcement, economic impact, and ethical consequences. The inclusion of meta and temporal traits reflects its recursive structure and dependence on time-limited protections.
